stories.headline: Defence Minister Pevkur caught in Middle East conflict zone during family vacation
stories.summary: Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur was on family vacation in Dubai when the US-Israel military operation against Iran began. He fled to Oman by land and eventually returned to Estonia, facing criticism for poor timing and significant additional costs. Despite the controversy, polling shows he remains the most trusted minister.

stories.headline: Foreign Minister Tsahkna says China and North Korea could be next regimes to be removed
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna stated at a government press conference that among Putin's allies, China and North Korea could be next in line to be removed from power, after others have already ended up 'in hell or prison.' The comments drew criticism as overly aggressive foreign policy.

stories.headline: South Korean defence company Hanwha Aerospace to invest 100 million euros in Estonia
stories.summary: Hanwha Aerospace announced a 100 million euro investment package in Estonian defence industry, including an ammunition factory and maintenance center. The investment is linked to Estonia's procurement of Chunmoo multiple rocket launchers and represents deeper defence cooperation with South Korea.

stories.headline: LHV Bank announces leadership change as Kadri Kiisel steps down
stories.summary: Estonia's LHV Bank announced that CEO Kadri Kiisel will step down from April 1, to be replaced by Erki Kilu, who previously led the Estonian bank before moving to run LHV's UK operations. The bank also announced dividend plans and reported strong growth over Kiisel's tenure.

stories.headline: Reform Party drops to fifth place in polling as support continues to decline
stories.summary: The governing Reform Party fell to fifth place in Norstat polling, losing 2.3 percentage points over four weeks and now polling practically even with EKRE at around 13%. The party is behind Isamaa, Center Party, Social Democrats and EKRE in the latest rankings.

stories.headline: Bank of Estonia reports economic indicators including wage growth and inflation data
stories.summary: Bank of Estonia released multiple economic reports showing 5.6% wage growth in 2025, continued inflation concerns, and improved business lending conditions. The central bank also addressed mortgage valuation rule changes and held seminars on payment fraud prevention.

stories.headline: Fuel prices rise in Estonia due to Middle East conflict impact on oil markets
stories.summary: Fuel prices at Estonian gas stations increased significantly due to rising oil prices following the escalation of conflict in the Middle East. Prices rose Monday and Tuesday, with some moderation later in the week as global oil markets fluctuated.
